text:
josh-customer: Hey support — our customer tenant `tenant-678` started getting 410 from /v1/rerank and every response returns scores [0,0,0]. No changes on our side. Example response below, can you help?

lisa-support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact request (model_id + headers) and a request_id if present?

josh-customer: Sure. Curl we used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model_id":"redwood/rerank-legacy-2022","inputs":["q1","q2"],"candidates":["a","b"]}'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 410 Gone` + body: `{ "error": "model_deprecated", "message": "model redwood/rerank-legacy-2022 has been retired" }`
Request-id header: `req_0a1b2c3d`

maria-eng: Noted. We did retire `redwood/rerank-legacy-2022` during the March cleanup. Normally aliases redirect but looks like this tenant is still sending the retired explicit model_id. Is this coming from a cached client?

kai-runtime: Quick checklist: 1) Is the client using an SDK that caches model mapping? 2) Any gateway/cache in front of the customer's service (CDN or proxy) that might hold old payloads? 3) Do we have the tenant mapping showing a redirect to `rerank-v2` or an alias? I can check routing if you give tenant id.

lisa-support: @josh-customer can you confirm whether you pass `model_id` (exact) or use an alias like `rerank/latest`? Also, do you see an `x-model-alias` response header in previous OK responses?

josh-customer: We're passing explicit `model_id` string (see curl). Our SDK was pinned to that string, not alias. Client was not updated. We assumed server-side redirect would work.

maria-eng: That explains it — explicit retired model_ids return 410. Alias redirects only apply when customers call alias names. Workaround: switch to alias `rerank/latest` or the new stable id `redwood/rerank-v2-2025`.

josh-customer: Can you confirm the new exact ID we should use? We need to ship a fix in today’s deploy.

kai-runtime: Use `redwood/rerank-v2-2025` (stable), or `rerank/latest` alias. Example working call:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model_id":"redwood/rerank-v2-2025","inputs":["q1","q2"],"candidates":["a","b"]}'
```
Expected: 200 + scores like `[0.74, 0.21]`.

lisa-support: I'll patch the support ticket with the workaround. @maria-eng can we add a short-lived redirect for explicit legacy IDs to reduce customer impact? Also want to know if any tenants still reference retired ids in our tenant config DB.

maria-eng: I don't want silent redirects for retired ids — risk of masking bugs. But we can add an audit/scan job to list tenants using retired ids and notify them. I'll open IR-4392 and run a quick query: `SELECT tenant_id FROM tenant_mappings WHERE model_id LIKE '%rerank-legacy%'` — results coming.

deploy-bot: [deployment] checked routing table for tenant-678 — mapping shows `model_alias: rerank/latest` (but SDK had hardcoded model_id). Cache TTL for admin mappings is 10m; edge SDK caches can be longer.

josh-customer: Confirmed — after changing to `redwood/rerank-v2-2025` in our staging SDK, rerank calls return 200 and sensible scores. Thanks.

lisa-support: Great. Action items: 1) maria to run tenant scan and open outreach list (IR-4392). 2) docs: add note about retired explicit model ids returning 410 vs alias behavior. 3) recommend customers prefer aliases or stable new model ids.

maria-eng: Opening IR-4392 now, will attach `req_0a1b2c3d` logs and tenant-678 mapping dump. ETA for outreach list: 24h.

lisa-support: Marking this thread resolved from support side. Reopen if you see anything else. :thumbsup:
